phrases.text: So welcome back again. Time for one more problem. Now, in this problem, we are given that if a man rides at thirty kilometer per hour,
he reaches at eleven AM. If he rides at forty kilometer per hour,
he reaches at
nine AM.
The question is asking us to find the speed at which he should ride so that
he reaches exactly at ten AM.
Now, let us assume the total distance is
d kilometer.
Be very sure about one thing.
The starting time remains the same in all three cases.
Only the speed changes,
so only the travel time changes.
Now, let us use the formula.
Time is equal to distance divided by speed.
So the time taken in the first case is
total distance divided by speed,
which is d divided by thirty. And the time taken in the second case is total distance divided by speed,
which is d divided by forty.
Now, the difference between the two arrival times is eleven AM minus nine AM,
which is two hours.
So we can write
d divided by thirty minus d divided by forty is equal to two.
After solving this equation, we get d is equal to two hundred and forty kilometers.
Now that we have found the total distance, we can find the starting time.
In the first case,
time taken is equal to total distance divided by speed.
That is equal to two hundred and forty divided by thirty.
This gives us eight hours.
Since he reaches at eleven AM,
the starting time is eleven AM minus eight hours.
That is equal to three AM.
Now this part is completed. We already know the starting time. To reach at ten AM,
the available travel time is from three AM to ten AM.
That is seven hours. Now we have everything we need. Required speed is equal to distance divided by time.
Putting the values,
required speed is equal to two hundred and forty divided by seven.
After simplifying this, we get thirty-four point two eight five seven kilometer per hour.
So the required speed is approximately thirty-four point two eight kilometer per hour.
Hence, the correct answer is
option D.
